lines: Eight-step pulse sequencer with an output for every step, a combined pattern output, and start, stop and clock outputs
Arms the sequencer, and playback then begins on the next rising clock edge; pressing it again halts playback at once
Chooses whether the pattern repeats indefinitely or stops when it reaches its endpoint, which is the last step of the pattern or an external reset
Chooses sequential playback, which plays the programmed pattern in order, or random playback, where the number of switched-on steps sets the chance of a pulse at PATTERN
Sets the length of the pulses at PATTERN: a gate matching the incoming clock pulse, or a fixed 10ms trigger
Switches that step of the pattern on or off, and in the other display modes the same button sets the loop count, the sequence length or the gate setting for that step
A pulse here starts playback when the sequencer is stopped and stops it when it is running
A pulse here restarts the pattern at its first step on the next clock pulse
Each rising edge advances the pattern by one step while the sequencer is running
A pulse here switches playback between sequential and random
Carries 5V on its own step: in sequential playback it follows the clock whether or not that step is switched on, and in random playback only when that step is on and the draw matches it
A 5V trigger 10ms long whenever playback starts
A 5V trigger 10ms long whenever playback stops
A copy of the signal at the CLOCK input, regenerated at 5V
The switched-on steps as one pulse stream at 5V, with the pulse length set by the GATE/TRIG button
Menu — Display modes — a heading over Grid programming, Loop repeats, Sequence length and Gate/trig settings, choosing what the eight step buttons show and set
Menu — Clock output — chooses Always active, so the CLOCK output carries the clock all the time, or During playback
Menu — Reset behavior — chooses Immediate, applying a reset the moment it arrives, or Queued, holding it back until the next clock pulse
Menu — Startup state: Start, Stop, Remember — sets the playback state the module takes when a patch is loaded
Menu — Step outputs — chooses Always active, so a step output pulses on its step whatever the pattern says, or Follow program, so it pulses only where that step is switched on
Note — Clock output, Reset behavior, Startup state and Step outputs are gathered under a User preferences heading in the same menu
Note — the module has no clock of its own; nothing advances until a clock is patched to CLOCK
Note — playback has to be started before PATTERN carries anything: press START/STOP, or send a pulse to STATE
Algorhythm.notes: The VCV build implements the original v1 Algorhythm firmware: one eight-step pattern with an output per step. The plugin's browser description and the Grayscale website describe the later 'Polyrhythm' v2 firmware, which turns the eight step outputs into eight independent channels; the VCV changelog for 1.0.0 says 'Update Algorhythm to the complete feature set of v1 firmware'. The hardware's hold-a-switch views are here as the Display modes menu.

lines: Looping random sequencer built on a 16-bit shift register, with a voltage sequence, an inverted copy of it, a gate output for each of the sixteen bits, white noise and a clock copy
Holds the sequence while it is pressed by disconnecting the clock, and playback carries on from where it stopped when it is released
Generates one internal clock pulse, moving the sequence forward by one bit
While it is held, the first bit of the shift register is set to zero on each clock pulse, turning ones into zeroes
While it is held, the first bit of the shift register is set to one on each clock pulse, turning zeroes into ones
Sets the chance the last bit is inverted as it is copied back to the first: even at the centre, none at LIN so the loop repeats unaltered, and inversion every time round at CYC, doubling the loop
Sets the bit the sequence is copied back from, 1 to 16, which is the length of the loop
Scales the voltage at SEQ and INV SEQ, from -8V fully counter-clockwise to 8V fully clockwise
Each rising edge moves the shift register on by one bit; it counts as high from 2V upwards
Adds to the SHIFT knob, 5V here covering the knob's full travel
Adds to the BITS knob, at three bits per volt
Adds to the LEVEL knob, and the result is limited to the range -8V to 8V
A voltage of 2V or more sets the first bit of the shift register to zero on the next clock pulse
A voltage of 2V or more sets the first bit of the shift register to one on the next clock pulse
The first eight bits of the shift register read as a number from 0 to 255 and scaled by LEVEL, giving a new voltage on every clock pulse
The voltage at SEQ with its sign flipped
White noise from the module's own generator, running whether or not a clock is patched
Carries 8V while the signal at the CLOCK input is high
Carries 8V while that bit of the shift register is a one, for as long as the clock pulse lasts
Note — the contents of the shift register are saved with the patch, so a locked sequence comes back when the patch is reopened
Note — the module has no clock of its own; the shift register moves only on a rising edge at CLOCK or a press of the STEP button
Permutation18.notes: The bit and clock outputs carry 8V here; the hardware manual says +10V pulses. The 8V figure is read from the compiled module. The noise output is a Gaussian generator scaled by three, not the hardware's calibrated 10V peak-to-peak analogue noise.

lines: Granular audio processor, an expanded version of Clouds by Mutable Instruments, with its own knob, CV input and attenuverter for each of nine parameters
Selects the point in the recording buffer the grains are played from; turning clockwise travels back in time
Sets the length of each grain
Transposes the grains; at the centre the buffer plays at the pitch it was recorded at
At the centre no grains are generated; clockwise from there they are sown at random, counter-clockwise from there at a steady rate
Morphs the grain envelope from a rectangle through a triangle to a raised cosine, and past about two o'clock brings in a diffuser that smears transients
Steps the recording buffer through 1, 2, 4 and 8 seconds, the sample rate falling as the time grows; the lamp for the chosen length blinks until the buffer is full
Stops new audio being written to the buffer, so the grains carry on playing from the material already there
Fires a single grain by hand
Steps through the four memory banks, loading the audio buffer stored in each
Silences the audio going into the buffer, and holds the red lamp of the input meter on
Silences the signal path ahead of the reverb, so reverb tails ring on rather than being cut off
Sets the level of the audio going into the buffer, reaching 6dB of gain fully clockwise, and sets the baseline that the input VCA voltage is added to
Sets how much of the processed output is written back into the buffer
Sets how widely the grains are scattered across the stereo field
Sets the balance between the dry input and the processed signal
Sets the amount of reverb on the output
Sets the final output level, reaching 6dB of gain fully clockwise, and sets the baseline that the output VCA voltage is added to
Attenuates and inverts the voltage reaching its parameter, from that parameter's own CV jack, from AUX, or from the internal random generator; at the centre no modulation gets through
A voltage added to the IN knob, changing the input level of both channels equally
A voltage added to the OUT knob, changing the output level of both channels equally
A gate here stops new audio being written to the buffer for as long as it is high
A pulse here fires a single grain
Transposes the grains exponentially, tracking one volt per octave, and is summed with the linear pitch CV
One voltage distributed to all nine parameters; a parameter whose own CV jack is patched takes that jack instead
The left audio input, which feeds both channels while the right input is empty
The right audio input
A voltage for that one parameter, scaled by that parameter's attenuverter, and it disconnects AUX and the internal random generator from that parameter
The left channel of the processed stereo output
The right channel of the processed stereo output
Note — the grains are played from a recording of whatever is patched to the audio inputs, so nothing comes out of the module until audio is patched in
Menu — Alternate mode — chooses Granular, Pitch-shifter/time-stretcher, Looping delay, Spectral madness, Oliverb, Resonestor, Beat repeat or Spectral clouds
Menu — Save buffer — writes the current contents of the recording buffer into one of the four banks, listed as Bank A to Bank D
Menu — Normalize AUX to random CV — switches the internal stepped 0-5V random generator on and off; while it is on and AUX is empty it reaches every parameter whose own CV jack is empty
Menu — Set random CV frequency from PAN knob — reads the PAN knob to set how fast the internal random voltage steps, 1Hz fully counter-clockwise and 100Hz fully clockwise
Note — with DENSITY at its centre no grains are generated at all, so the module passes the dry signal and nothing else
Note — the recording buffer has to fill before the grains have material to play; the lamp for the chosen TIME length blinks until it has
Supercell.notes: The IN and OUT knobs are logarithmic, 0 to 6dB with unity at the default position, read from the compiled module. The hardware sets the playback algorithm by holding TIME and the random CV rate by holding TRIG while turning PAN; in the plugin both are menu items. The hardware's four save banks are operated from the BANK button and the Save buffer menu item.

lines: Twelve-channel macro controller: a keyframe stores the levels of all twelve VCAs at one point on a timeline, and the large knob moves along that timeline, interpolating between the keyframes
Chooses which channels the AMP knob edits, and clicking it moves the selection scope on to the next of one channel, a column of two, and all twelve
Sets the level of the channels in the selection scope at the current keyframe, and clicking it flips those channels between their lowest and highest levels
Moves along the timeline, interpolating levels between the keyframes on either side; VCA levels can be edited only while it points at a keyframe
Inverts the levels of the channels in the selection scope at the current keyframe, and pressing it again puts them back
Adds a keyframe at the current timeline position, or deletes the keyframe already there
Normals an internal 10V offset to every channel input with nothing patched, so those channels generate control voltages instead of passing an external signal
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the MOD input before it moves the timeline, and at the centre no modulation gets through
Audio or control voltage into that channel's VCA; each odd-numbered input is normalled to the even-numbered input beside it, so one cable fills a stereo pair
Moves the timeline, added to the position of the large knob and scaled by the MOD attenuator; in the two sequencer modes a trigger here moves to the next keyframe
That channel's input after its VCA, and patching it subtracts that channel from the mix output for its row
A 10ms trigger each time a keyframe becomes active
The mix of the odd-numbered channel outputs, without any channel whose own output jack is patched
The mix of the even-numbered channel outputs, without any channel whose own output jack is patched
Note — the maker's manual says at least two keyframes are needed before there is anything to interpolate; turn the timeline knob to a position, press KEY, move to another position and press KEY again
Menu — Selection scope — chooses Single, Columns or All for which channels the AMP knob edits
Menu — Sequencing mode — chooses Keyframer, which interpolates between keyframes, Sequencer (step), which moves on one keyframe at a trigger, or Sequencer (random)
Menu — Interpolation curve — chooses Linear, Exponential, Logarithmic, Sine, Step A or Step B for how the selected channels travel between keyframes
Menu — VCA response — chooses Linear, 25%, 50%, 75% or Exponential for how the level of the selected channels follows the AMP knob
Menu — Copy keyframe — takes the levels of the keyframe at the timeline position now, and Paste keyframe writes them at whatever position is reached next
Menu — Randomize levels — gives every channel in the selection scope a new random level at the current keyframe
Menu — Delete all keyframes — empties the timeline and returns every channel to linear interpolation and linear response
Menu — Factory presets — a submenu of twelve worked examples, from Null (no keyframes) and Min/max fader through the submixes and crossfaders to Six CV/gate sequencers
Menu — Toggle min/max levels — flips the channels in the selection scope between their lowest and highest levels, which is what clicking the AMP knob does
Menu — Invert levels — inverts the levels of the channels in the selection scope, which is what the VAR button does
Note — the AMP knob changes nothing while the timeline knob points between keyframes; move it onto a keyframe, or add one with KEY, before editing levels
Nexus.notes: The channel inputs and outputs carry whatever is patched to them, audio or control voltage, so they are left without a family. The hardware reaches the selection scope, sequencing mode, interpolation curve, VCA response, preset save and load, copy and paste, randomisation and LED brightness through long presses and combinations of SEL, AMP, VAR and KEY; in the plugin these are menu items, and the 12 factory presets are one of them. The compiled module offers three selection scopes, single, columns and all, where the hardware manual also lists rows. Firmware update, VCA calibration and LED brightness have no counterpart here.
